newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn losses pared late on commercial spread.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn losses pared late on commercial spread.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended lower but losses were limited late by commercial bull spreading, traders said.
Continental Grain reportedly bull spread four million bushels March/July and three million bushels March/May.
The move suggested nearby demand was strengthening.
"Continental was a good bull spreader today and people now think there will not be a buildup of stocks in Toledo and Chicago," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Corn had struggled earlier as commercials sold but traders noted ADM and Term Commodities were net buyers on the day.
ADM repotedly bought three million bushels March and Term Commodities bought 2.5 million bushels March on the day.
Options trading was also active as Prudential Securities bought 1,500 March $2.60 puts and sold 1,500 March $2.90 calls at 3/4 and 1/2 cents per bushels, traders said.
Prudential also bought 500 March $2.50 puts and sold another 500 March $2.90 calls, traders said.

New crop corn contracts were depressed by reports that Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies had forecast U.S. corn planted area this year at 81.5 million acres, slightly higher than some trade expectations.
"The Sparks corn number was a little high and that put a little pressure on December corn," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
USDA estimated 1996 U.S. corn planted area at 79.5 million acres.
Corn closed steady to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower with March unchanged at $2.73-1/4.
Volume was estimated at 48,000 contracts, against Thursday's actual volume of 69,222 contracts.
